challenges.headline: Check-in treated as one boolean action
challenges.premise: The request frames 'check attendees in' as a single scan-and-done action.
challenges.alternative: A second scan of the same attendee can mean a blocked duplicate, an allowed re-entry, or access to a different zone/session — three different data models, not one flag.
challenges.consequence: Building a simple boolean check-in now means a data-model rebuild later, with no second chance since the event date cannot move.
challenges.recommendation: Pin down the exact check-in semantics (duplicate vs re-entry vs multi-zone) with the client before designing the data model.

challenges.headline: Reliable connectivity assumed
challenges.premise: The request describes staff scanning at the entrance with no mention of network conditions, implying the venue's wifi/4G will simply work.
challenges.alternative: Venues routinely have dead zones and saturated networks; the standard pattern is offline-first with a local snapshot and check-ins syncing later.
challenges.consequence: Discovering the connectivity gap on-site or late in build forces an architecture change under time pressure, on an event day that cannot be rescheduled.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm connectivity at the actual venue (ideally via a site visit) before committing to an online-only or offline-first design.

challenges.headline: Single-event scope taken for granted
challenges.premise: The request reads as a one-off app for this event, with no mention of future events.
challenges.alternative: Clients running one event commonly return for the next one; a single-event build then has to be retrofitted into a multi-event, configurable kit.
challenges.consequence: Building single-event-only now risks a full rebuild of the data model and configuration layer the moment a second event is requested.
challenges.recommendation: Ask the client directly whether more events are planned before locking the data model and configuration approach.

challenges.headline: One-off build vs reusable kit
challenges.premise: The request reads as a single-event feature with no stated position on whether it needs to work again for future events.
challenges.alternative: Many clients running one event today run several a year; this fork changes configurability, the data model (single-event vs multi-event) and cost, and is worth settling before anything else.
challenges.consequence: Guessing wrong means either over-engineering configurability nobody needed, or a throwaway build that gets rebuilt from scratch for the next event.
challenges.recommendation: Ask the client directly whether this is a one-off or the first instance of a reusable event kit before any architecture decision is made.

challenges.headline: Reliable connectivity assumed
challenges.premise: The request implies staff simply scan attendees in, with no mention of venue network conditions.
challenges.alternative: Event venues routinely have basements, thick walls and saturated wifi; offline-first (local snapshot, deferred sync, conflict rules) is the realistic domain default, not an edge case.
challenges.consequence: Building online-only and discovering the venue's connectivity gap on event day is unrecoverable — there's no next sprint, only a queue at the door in front of the client.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm venue connectivity and offline requirements now, and budget a rehearsal on real hardware in the real venue as part of scope.

challenges.headline: Check-in treated as a boolean
challenges.premise: 'Check attendees in' is being taken as a single yes/no event per attendee.
challenges.alternative: In this domain a second scan routinely means a duplicate (block), a re-entry (allow), or access to a different zone/session (record separately) — three different data models, not one flag.
challenges.consequence: Locking in a boolean check-in model now means a costly data-model migration later if zones, sessions or re-entry turn out to matter.
challenges.recommendation: Clarify with the client what a repeat scan should mean before designing the Check-in entity.
